# GitHub release API evidence

Captured on 2026-10-17 from the current authenticated GitHub CLI session. All repository reads were explicitly scoped; no secrets, environment settings, or release records were changed.

## Captured responses

- `github_run_list.json`: `gh run list --repo Artypoul/Flashco --workflow build.yaml --commit 83089903cc33bbfb720af5e7ec37ba58cef5474e --limit 50 --json databaseId,workflowName,headSha,event,status,conclusion,createdAt,updatedAt,url` returned one completed successful push run, ID `38913914849`, with head SHA `83089903cc33bbfb720af5e7ec37ba58cef5474e`.
- `github_run_view.json`: `gh run view 38913914849 --repo Artypoul/Flashco --json databaseId,workflowName,headSha,event,status,conclusion,createdAt,updatedAt,url,jobs` returned the run plus all 11 jobs. `build` and `upload` were skipped; the other nine jobs concluded successfully. Job step fields retain the CLI response's actual string, integer, timestamp, and array types.
- `github_releases_own.json`: `gh api --paginate repos/Artypoul/Flashco/releases` completed successfully and returned JSON `[]`, so the complete visible release history was empty at capture time.
- `github_run_artifacts.json`: `gh api --paginate repos/Artypoul/Flashco/actions/runs/38913914849/artifacts` completed successfully and returned `{"total_count":0,"artifacts":[]}`. The selected `build.yaml` run left no Actions artifacts to recover.
- `github_donor_run_artifacts.json`: `gh api --paginate repos/chen08209/FlClash/actions/runs/38494931447/artifacts` returned seven real artifact records from the donor's successful `v0.9.0` run. The fixture keeps identifiers, names, sizes, expiry state, digest, timestamps, and nested `workflow_run` identity fields; download URLs and unneeded API links are omitted.
- `github_release_donor.json`: `gh api 'repos/chen08209/FlClash/releases?per_page=1'` returned a published `v0.9.0` release with 16 uploaded assets. Only actual release metadata and selected asset metadata are retained. Release body, uploader profiles, API upload URL, and unrelated repository links are omitted. Retained browser download URLs are public links from the donor's live release.

The JSON fixtures are deliberately compact projections of real successful responses; no payload values or field types were fabricated. They are adequate evidence for the release list, run/job, release boolean, asset-list, and downloadable asset metadata shapes. They do not model draft responses or API error responses.

The artifact record fields were compared with GitHub's [List workflow run artifacts](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/artifacts#list-workflow-run-artifacts) response schema. The donor response is the nonempty observed example; the Flashco run response is the observed empty case.

## API and workflow constraints from GitHub documentation

- Release creation requires repository `Contents: write`; the request must set `draft: true` explicitly because the API default is published. GitHub documents that a create-release request may return 404 (or in some authentication paths 403) when its target commit adds/modifies `.github/workflows/` relative to the default branch and the token cannot modify workflows. GitHub says `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot be granted this workflow authorization. Check the exact release target against the default branch before treating that response as a permission failure: [Create a release](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases#create-a-release).
- Release assets are uploaded using the release response's `upload_url`; the returned asset has `name`, `state`, `size`, `content_type`, `digest`, and `browser_download_url` fields. Asset upload permission follows release contents write access: [Upload a release asset](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/assets#upload-a-release-asset).
- Workflow `permissions` can reduce the token to only the scopes needed, and when any scope is explicitly listed, omitted scopes are set to `none`. The release job needs `contents: write`; read-only jobs can retain `contents: read`: [Workflow permissions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#permissions).
- GitHub concurrency permits only one active run per group. By default, a new pending run replaces an older pending run; `queue: max` allows up to 100 pending runs, while `cancel-in-progress: true` also cancels the active run. For a release workflow, serialize by a stable group, use `queue: max`, and keep cancellation false so a later manual run does not interrupt an active upload or replace an earlier queued release: [Concurrency](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#concurrency).
- An environment can gate a job with reviewers or other protection rules and release environment secrets only after the rules pass. This is optional for the planned draft-only workflow and does not replace an explicit operator approval to publish: [Deployment environments](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/deployment-environments).

Capture establishes a read-only empty public history, but does not prove that the new workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` will be allowed to create a release for every future target SHA. The release creation check must use the exact selected SHA after the workflow lands in the default branch; do not probe it by creating a draft as part of this evidence capture.

## 4C run provenance and not-found response

Captured on 2026-10-17 from the current authenticated GitHub CLI session. The read was explicitly scoped to `Artypoul/Flashco`; only selected public fields were retained.

- `github_run_provenance.json` is a projection of `gh api repos/Artypoul/Flashco/actions/runs/38913914849 --jq '{id,event,head_branch,head_sha,path,workflow_id,run_attempt,status,conclusion,display_title,name,run_number,created_at,updated_at}'`. The response has integer `id`, `workflow_id`, `run_attempt`, and `run_number`; selected remaining values are strings for this completed run. `event` is `push`, `head_branch` is `main`, `head_sha` is `83089903cc33bbfb720af5e7ec37ba58cef5474e`, and `path` is `.github/workflows/build.yaml`. This observed run is not a release-workflow run.
- `github_release_tag_not_found.json` is the body from `gh api --include --method GET 'repos/Artypoul/Flashco/releases/tags/v99999999.99999999.99999999'`. GitHub returned HTTP 404 with `message`, `documentation_url`, and string `status`. The response headers and CLI stderr are omitted.
- GitHub documents `run-name` as the name shown for a workflow run, supports expressions from the `inputs` context, and says the event-specific title is used when omitted. Therefore, for a future workflow configured with a tag-specific `run-name`, `display_title` is the observable REST field to correlate with the requested tag; `name` is the workflow name. Correlation still must validate the REST `path`, `workflow_id`, `event`, `head_branch`, `head_sha`, and job/artifact provenance before recovery. A missing artifact cannot be treated as proof that no partial release write occurred.

Sources: [workflow syntax (`run-name`)](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#run-name), [REST API for workflow runs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs?apiVersion=2026-03-10), [REST API for release lookup by tag](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases#get-a-release-by-tag-name).

The run-list REST envelope is also captured in `github_build_runs_api.json` from `gh api 'repos/Artypoul/Flashco/actions/workflows/385298741/runs?head_sha=83089903cc33bbfb720af5e7ec37ba58cef5474e&per_page=100' --jq '{total_count,workflow_runs: [.workflow_runs[] | {id,event,head_branch,head_sha,path,workflow_id,run_attempt,status,conclusion,display_title,name,run_number,created_at,updated_at}]}'`. Its observed shape is an integer `total_count` and `workflow_runs` array of run objects with integer IDs/attempts and string provenance/status fields. This is a one-run successful real response, not a release workflow example.

The job REST envelope in `github_build_jobs_api.json` is from `gh api 'repos/Artypoul/Flashco/actions/runs/38913914849/jobs?per_page=100' --jq '{total_count, jobs: [.jobs[] | {id,name,status,conclusion,started_at,completed_at,run_attempt}]}'`. It is a real 11-job response; the nine required checks succeeded and the `build`/`upload` jobs were skipped. This records actual job-attempt and interval field types for provenance checks, but is not a release bundle-job record.
